content.comment_body: The quoted duration for memory backup during power loss is 80 hours at 25°C. We need this to last at least 90 days to keep the hour counter intact. Is there a way to achieve this, apart from modifying the device's memory circuit with an extra lithium cell? Any advice is appreciated!

There is no battery module available for [product_name]. The program itself is saved in internal non-volatile memory, but data retention lasts only several hours when power is lost. The only workaround is to prevent extended power outages. For larger systems like [product_name], data retentive during power-off periods longer than several hours requires a battery module, which can last about 200 days. If you require 90 days of power-off time, you'd need to replace the battery after two cycles of 90 days. Additional details and order numbers are listed in the relevant manual chapters.

Could you please clarify: If I have a program stored in [product_name] and lose power, what gets lost? Is it just the program and parameters? If I use a colored memory chip, does that ensure safety beyond 80 hours, or is the program still deleted after a few hours? I appreciate suggestions to prevent losing my program, which operates a large aquarium system.

Dear customer, your program in [product_name] is stored safely in the internal non-volatile memory, so it survives a power interruption. Block parameters are also saved if marked as retentive; otherwise, they are lost during power loss. External memory modules serve for copying, transferring, or backing up your program. The internal clock is only buffered after power failure for about 80 hours under standard conditions. Your technical support team.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is searching for a way to extend memory retention during power outages on [product_name] to preserve runtime data for up to 90 days. Replies explain that while program storage is non-volatile and unaffected by outages, runtime values such as clocks and counters are only kept for around 80 hours. Since the device lacks an official battery backup module, upgrading to a higher-end product with battery support is suggested.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to retain both program and operational data—especially the hour counter—during long-term power interruptions for up to 90 days without loss. The user hopes external memory solutions or alternative methods can ensure this level of backup.
